decisions.summary: _trim_to_service loses its two vertex-popping loops; the existing two-pass 4 ft walk is the one pull-back for every end, popping a vertex only once the end is within 4 ft of it; the comment above the walk is rewritten to say so; the claim line stands unchanged.
decisions.why: This is 385 T126, an open non-process task moved into 405 by the GM's routing ('everything else moves into a new feature') and worked as 385 worked its tasks (FR-001). It brings the code into line with its own unchanged claim and the 0246 research ('pulled back to the last house it serves'), which the impl-drift round recorded DRIFTED. Nothing the request or the spec asks for is narrowed: no end, lane or case is excluded, and the claim is not weakened.

decisions.summary: Exit (e) conform the code to the claim rather than amend the claim; a coarser walk step was weighed and refused, keeping the existing 4 ft grain.
decisions.why: Conforming to the stated claim and research keeps existing documented behavior the request does not touch; refusing a coarser step changes nothing and carves out no case.

decisions.summary: A unit test red at HEAD on a run whose long last segment passes a house within 60 ft partway; claims round on the changed unit; gate and landing cohort.
decisions.why: Verification that only fails when the fixed behavior is absent - enforcement of the task, plus the standing 385 per-task checks FR-001 carries; no new behavior, map or tier is added.

decisions.summary: The plan is written one section per task, each at that task's start, against docs/approach-checklist.md.
decisions.why: A drafting convention for the plan document; it narrows nothing the request or FR-001 (each task worked as 385 worked its tasks, checklist part A answered) asks for.

decisions.summary: Lands open: T01-T31 - the feature may reach main with any of its 31 tasks still open.
decisions.why: The GM's 2026-10-20 start asks for one claim fixed and then the numbers reviewed before deciding what next (FR-004, SC-002: a report before a second task), so landing with the remaining tasks open is what was asked. Declaring a task may land open does not drop it: SC-001 still requires every task ticked, and no task is removed or exempted from FR-001/FR-002.

## T31 - task-add numbers a task from the boxes' own ids (found working T12)
## T32 - only the task being worked holds a landing (the GM, 2026-10-20)

decisions.summary: plan_bundle.build refuses (SystemExit, naming specs/<name>/request.md and what goes in it) before writing a bundle when request.md is missing
decisions.why: A finding on code T12 did not change, filed as a task of this feature as FR-002 and the GM's 2026-10-19 words ('keep findings on code a task didn't change as new tasks') require; it makes a plan review read the GM's words verbatim, which is the review's own contract.

decisions.summary: building request.md from the spec's quote was weighed and refused
decisions.why: Keeps the review on the GM's verbatim words rather than a possibly trimmed quote; narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: task-add next_id takes the largest id of tasks.md boxes and plan.md/plan-done.md '## T<n>' headings, plus one, ignoring ids quoted in titles
decisions.why: FR-002 found work; conforms task-add to 385 T64 D83's 'next free id' instead of reading quoted ids such as '(385 T147)'.

decisions.summary: only the clone's active task (plan_gate.active_task) of this feature, open and not in L7R_LAND_TICKS, holds a push; GM-review box, carried and unstarted tasks never hold; the push's refusal names the active task and 'make land F= T='
decisions.why: Directly answers the GM's 2026-10-20 'I do not want each landing to owe a lands open line ... that's going to slow things down', while keeping 330's protection of mid-task work. 375 D12's effect (the GM-review box does not hold a landing) is preserved. Residual, not a ruling: the hold reaches mid-task work only when 'make task-start' was run in the clone, so the mechanism's reach depends on task-start being required before work.

decisions.summary: the **Lands open**: line is no longer read; task-add stops writing it and the [lands-open] mark; the tick's 'mark the tooling did not put here' refusal is removed and any mark is inert text
decisions.why: The consequence of the GM's 'no lands open line': with only the active task holding, the line, the mark and the refusal that policed the mark have nothing left to do. The tick's refusal guarded self-exemption through a mark that no longer exempts anything.

decisions.summary: keeping the line without its review was weighed and refused
decisions.why: The GM asked for no line at all; keeping it would be the thing he declined.

decisions.summary: scripts/land.py / make land: pass 1 prints every cheap refusal (tick refusals but the landed one, uncommitted work, owed ledger rows, claims gate, review gate, holding rule) together and exits 2; pass 2 runs gate-stamp check, 'make done' when the stamp does not cover the content, 'make cohort-landing' when the cohort gate refuses, commits gate regenerations under pool/, pushes with L7R_LAND_TICKS, ticks each task; land-batch.py a shim
decisions.why: Answers the GM's 'the landing being the biggest cost is something that we need to do something about' and his ask to make and work the tooling changes. Every gate still runs and still refuses; only the order and the hand steps between them change. Auto-running make done / cohort-landing and committing their pool/ output does what the session did by hand after each refusal; no gate is skipped.

decisions.summary: running the gate and the cohort in parallel deferred to a measurement of its own (memory cap, feature 315)
decisions.why: A deferral of one option, not a narrowing of anything the GM asked; nothing requested is removed.

decisions.summary: in push_cmd the fetch, the delta, the holding rule and review-gate.sh run before push_checks.py and claims-gate.sh; checks and messages otherwise unchanged
decisions.why: Reorder only, serving the GM's landing-cost ask; the holding rule is still judged against the fetched main. D6 moves claims-gate.sh behind as well, which approach item 5 does not name but item 4's current-order note implies; no check is dropped.

decisions.summary: sync-with-main.sh done runs push_cmd then render_sync_background (lock and log as the prompt hook's), printing where the log is; render-sync stays foreground for a hand run
decisions.why: Render-sync still runs after every landing, so the GM's 2026-08-12 reason (renders in main kept fresh) is kept; only the landing stops waiting on it, which is the GM's 2026-10-20 landing-cost ask. Residual: a session must not tell the GM to look at a render until the background log shows it finished, or the 2026-08-12 round trip recurs.
